version.changelog: Synced with kubectl-mcp-server 2.0: tool names and arguments match the 2.0 toolsets; each skill lists the toolsets it needs.

llm.summary: This Kubernetes management skill needs review because its examples insufficiently scope secret transfers and production cluster changes.

dimensions.detail: Both guides retrieve secrets at namespace scope and illustrate applying a secret manifest to another cluster without defining permitted secrets or checking destination trust. Explicit source and target contexts help targeting, but leave sensitive transfer authorization under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundle contains two Markdown guides requiring separately configured kubectl-mcp-server toolsets. No bundled installer, executable payload, or concealed download instruction was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md lines 135–139 scale a production-named machine deployment without specifying the management-cluster context, contradicting its explicit-context rule. Broad activation keywords are imprecise, but do not independently establish unauthorized execution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Saving retrieved cluster credentials locally is disclosed. Separate credentials, read-only production access, and auditing are recommended; no hidden persistence or privilege escalation is evidenced. These safeguards do not fully resolve the secret-transfer and scaling examples.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Context management, kubeconfig access, cluster lifecycle operations, Helm, and GitOps fit the disclosed purpose. The advisory scanner's credential-theft and GitOps mismatch claims are not supported by the artifacts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Start with narrowly scoped, read-only cluster access. Before allowing changes, verify the exact cluster, namespace, resource, and intended operation. Authorize individual secrets and trusted destinations before transfer, protect saved kubeconfigs, and keep secret values out of responses and logs. See [Kubernetes Secrets guidance](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/secrets-good-practices/). The artifacts support operational review concerns, without evidence of malicious intent.
